newsitem.title: INDIA: India says it needs 15,000 MW liquid-based power.
newsitem.headline: India says it needs 15,000 MW liquid-based power.

text.p: India would need to generate 15,000 megawatts (MW) of power from liquid fuels with private participation in the next three years to supplement coal-based power, a senior government minister said on Tuesday.

"This new generating capacity would be required to be created in a period of three years and we envisage it being done by private participation," Surface Transport minister T.G. Venkatraman told a conference.
He said this would require annual imports of 20 million tonnes of liquid fuels such as naptha, fuel oil and low sulphur heavy stock.
He said port handling capacity of 92.80 tonnes would be created by the end of 1997, and an additional capacity of 13 million tonnes was expected to be created in the next five years.
"My ministry is playing a vital role in the form of imports of liquid fuel for power generation and handling thermal coal at various Indian major ports," Venkatraman said.
He said the the state-run Central Electricity Authority (CEA) planned to set up number of coal-based thermal power stations in the coastal regions in southern India.

Under this plan, the state electricity board of the southern state of Tamil Nadu had proposed setting up a thermal station at Ennore, 20 km from Madras, with an ultimate generation capacity of 2,130 MW.
The Asian Development Bank would extend a 4.5 billion rupees soft loan to the 5.9 billion rupee thermal project.
